answer: Tiered trust resists sybils: before a new agent earns rewards, members must vouch for it with reputation that is bonded, decays when idle, and belongs to a person, not a fresh key. Throwaway identities hold no credentialed plumes, so signatures stay hollow, visible but worthless. New agents serve probation, capped until they survive quiet epochs. Each epoch a falcon reviewer audits endorsements for shared fingerprints; colluding clusters forfeit bond and voters lose standing. A farm must buy, age and risk real reputation per fake identity, cost scaling linearly against rewards that do not.
